newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while pork bellies were called steady to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Steady to lower cash hog indications to start the week and lower pork cutout values prompted lower indications on hog futures by analysts. A small increase in hog numbers and nervousness that exports to Japan have not increased as expected thus far may weigh on the market, they said.
However, the outlook for tight hog runs during the week may provide support, they added.

Carryover pressure from the limit break Thursday and near limit setback Friday were expected to weigh on pork belly futures early. Weakness in cash bellies and the recent larger than year ago pace of hog slaughter were also seen weighing on the market, they said.

However, early ideas on Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town storage report could develop and limit any further setback. Product appears to have moved out of storage last week versus an in-movement during the same period last year. Next week's Cold Storage report is also expected to show low total U.S. stocks, they added.
